name: Ming-3.0-tts-0.5B
purpose: Dense 0.5B multilingual speech synthesis with paralinguistic and free-form control: zero-shot voice cloning, voice design from a text description, 14 inline sound tags, emotion/speed/pitch/volume control (card).

license.name: MIT
license.notes: LICENSE of the sibling Ming-3.0-asr-tiny repo (same inclusionAI MIT notice, Copyright 2026 inclusionAI) read; this repo's card header says license: mit. This repo's own LICENSE file was not opened separately.

architecture.kind: dense autoregressive backbone with DiT head, audio tokenizer and speaker encoder (44.1 kHz output)
architecture.why_this_design: Card gives no reasons; the 0.5B name refers to the Qwen2.5-0.5B backbone, the HF API counts 1.48B parameters in total (backbone plus DiT head, tokenizer, speaker encoder).

variants.notes: HF API sum of files; inference needs the GitHub repo inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts

other: Python reference (ming_tts.MingTTS, CLI infer.py; tested on NVIDIA H800 and H20 with CUDA 12.4, SDPA fallback without flash-attn)
engine_support.notes: Card says the HF repo is checkpoint distribution only; a DiT head needs a diffusion step loop that is not in llama.cpp.

benchmarks.name: German WER on MiniMax TTS-Multilingual-Test-Set (SIM 0.753)
benchmarks.harness: ASR-based WER, unified protocol, recommended settings per model (card)

benchmarks.name: Spanish WER on MiniMax test set (SIM 0.763)
French WER on MiniMax test set (SIM 0.675)

strengths: German WER 0.365% on the builder's multilingual set, close to the larger tiny sibling (0.325%)
Voice cloning, voice design and free-form style from one small checkpoint
weaknesses: German speaker similarity 0.753 is below the tiny sibling (0.791)
French WER 4.3% is weaker than the tiny sibling (3.5%)
Inline sound tags are documented for Chinese and English only
best_for: small local TTS with German and cloning where a diffusion head is acceptable
soft.maturity: Ant Group Ming family; 18k downloads on the HF API on 2026-11-19.

tona_fit.reason: MIT, German officially supported, 3 GB, so it fits every hardware class easily and is the smallest Ming option; the 0.5B vs tiny trade is quality for size and needs a listening test. A Qwen2.5 backbone plus DiT head is a modest port compared with Ling MoE.
blockers: DiT head and audio tokenizer not in Tona

sources.note: MIT text of the sibling repo

open_questions: Latency and RTF (not on the card)
Own LICENSE file of this repo not opened
